text:
Two dice give $36$ equally likely outcomes. The possible sums range from $2$ to $12$, and the prime sums in that range are $2, 3, 5, 7, 11$.

Counting the ways to get each prime sum:

| Sum | Ways | Outcomes |
|-----|------|----------|
| 2 | 1 | (1,1) |
| 3 | 2 | (1,2), (2,1) |
| 5 | 4 | (1,4), (2,3), (3,2), (4,1) |
| 7 | 6 | (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) |
| 11 | 2 | (5,6), (6,5) |

That gives $1 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 2 = 15$ favourable outcomes.

$$P(\text{sum is prime}) = \frac{15}{36} = \frac{5}{12} \approx 0.417$$
